    tempest_fastapi_sdk.geo¶

    Geolocalização sem API paga: distância, rotas, geometria e geocoding.

    « Web, UI e utilitários

    geo ¶

    Geolocation — distance, routing, geometry and geocoding, no paid API.

    Layers, all sharing the same schemas:

    • Offline math (zero deps, zero network): :func:haversine_km and the spatial helpers in :mod:geometry (:func:bounding_box, :func:within_radius, :func:nearest, :func:destination_point, :func:initial_bearing, :func:point_in_polygon, :func:polygon_area_km2, :func:path_length_km), plus :func:estimate_travel for a road distance / per-mode time.
    • Real routing (free, open-source): :class:OSRMBackend for routes, routes through stops (:meth:OSRMBackend.route_through, with :func:estimate_route_through as the offline fallback), route geometry and distance/duration matrices; :class:NominatimBackend for forward/reverse geocoding. Both take an injected httpx.AsyncClient (install the [geo] extra for httpx); the rest imports without it.
    • Caching: :class:CachedGeocodingBackend wraps any :class:GeocodingBackend in front of a pluggable :class:GeocodeCacheStore — :class:InMemoryGeocodeCacheStore for tests and dev, :class:RedisGeocodeCacheStore for a shared Redis.
    • Live position: :class:LivePositionStore keeps the latest :class:LivePositionSchema per channel in Redis (throttle, least movement, TTL, :meth:LivePositionStore.clear) and delivers accepted positions over an SSE broker to the recipients an audience callback names, optionally with each one's ETA; :func:make_live_position_router receives them behind mandatory authorize and channel_active dependencies.
    • Fleet traffic: :class:RoadGraph (from an OSM excerpt with :func:road_graph_from_overpass / :func:load_road_graph), :func:match_to_roads (HMM map-matching, a port of tempest-react-sdk's), :class:TrafficAggregator (median speed per road stretch, published only k-anonymously, start and end of every trip cut, rotating hashes) and :func:make_traffic_router; map-matching quality per window, k-anonymous (quality= + :func:make_match_quality_router); :class:OffRoadDensity + :func:infer_road_candidates turn off-road density into road candidates for human review.
    • Database: :class:GeoPointMixin (model) + :class:GeoRepositoryMixin (portable radius search) / :class:PostGISRepositoryMixin (ST_DWithin).
    • Database, paginated: :meth:GeoRepositoryMixin.paginate_nearby computes :func:haversine_distance_sql in SQL and pages there, each item a :class:NearbyMatch (row, distance_km).
    • Brazil: :func:uf_centroid (offline state centres), :func:cep_to_coordinate (CEP via a geocoder), :func:extract_cep (CEP from free text) and :func:resolve_br_coordinate (CEP → address → state centroid). Every IBGE municipality offline, with code and coordinate: :func:municipality_by_ibge_code, :func:search_municipalities (typos included) and :func:find_municipalities_in_text ("moro em sao jose dos campos - sp").

    Motorcycle/bus/bicycle/pedestrian are derived from the car result by scaling the duration (see :data:DEFAULT_MODE_DURATION_FACTORS).

    CEP_PATTERN module-attribute ¶

    CEP_PATTERN: Pattern[str] = re.compile('\\b(\\d{5})-?(\\d{3})\\b')

    A CEP written anywhere in free text, with or without the dash.

    DEFAULT_GEOCODE_CACHE_PRECISION module-attribute ¶

    DEFAULT_GEOCODE_CACHE_PRECISION: int = 3

    Decimal places a reverse coordinate is rounded to before keying.

    Three places is a ~111 m grid (measured with :func:~tempest_fastapi_sdk.geo.haversine_km at 10⁻³ of a degree of latitude); more places fragment the cache without making the answer better, since a street resolves to the same building.

    DEFAULT_GEOCODE_CACHE_TTL_SECONDS module-attribute ¶

    DEFAULT_GEOCODE_CACHE_TTL_SECONDS: int = 2592000

    Default entry lifetime: 30 days.

    Long enough that a whole device fleet settles into hits, short enough that a map edit or a corrected place reaches users within a month. Place resolutions are stable on that horizon — the coordinates of a doorway do not move — while a week would re-buy quota every month and "forever" would pin a wrong answer.

    ROAD_MATCH_DEFAULTS module-attribute ¶

    ROAD_MATCH_DEFAULTS: Final[RoadMatchOptions] = RoadMatchOptions()

    Default tuning: sigma 7 m, beta 3 m, radius 200 m, 16 roads, detour 100 m, plus 2 m of detour per second between timed fixes, capped at 60 s.

    Ported from tempest-react-sdk's ROAD_MATCH_DEFAULTS, chosen there by sweeping every knob on the Kubicka et al. dataset (100 real drives, 247 251 fixes, node scripts/bench-map-matching.mjs): 92.33% of fixes on the right road, 98.53% without the three drives through yards missing from OSM.

    detour_per_second_m and max_interval_s were chosen there on the same drives thinned to one fix every 5-300 s and on public OpenStreetMap traces of five Brazilian city centres (node scripts/bench-br-osm.mjs, PR #678): 2 m/s is the largest rate that leaves the 1 Hz result where it was, and a 60 s cap keeps the long gaps of a 1 Hz trace from widening the search.

    Belo Horizonte, São Paulo, Florianópolis, Porto Alegre, Brasília, João Pessoa, São José dos Campos and Rio de Janeiro. A short list on purpose: every entry is a word most Brazilians read as that city. In a text it is a one-word name like any other, so it needs a sign of being a place — a locative cue before it ("vou pra bh"), an uppercase first letter ("Rio"), a state after it, or being the whole text ("bh") — and "o bh do time" scores below the default min_score.

    DEFAULT_DENSITY_BLOCK_CELLS module-attribute ¶

    DEFAULT_DENSITY_BLOCK_CELLS: Final[int] = 5

    Side of a k-anonymity block, in cells: 5 x 5 m = 25 m.

    k is decided per block, not per 5 m cell: with GPS noise a device spreads its points over several cells across the road, so k distinct devices in one 5 m cell is rare where k in a 25 m block is not. Measured on the synthetic street of scripts/bench_geo_traffic.py (k 5, sigma 5 m): deciding per cell, 20 trips a day gave no candidate and 40 recovered the street; per block, 12 trips recover 77% of it and 20 all of it. Counts stay per cell.

    CachedGeocodingBackend ¶

    CachedGeocodingBackend(
    *,
    backend: GeocodingBackend,
    store: GeocodeCacheStore,
    precision: int = DEFAULT_GEOCODE_CACHE_PRECISION,
    ttl_seconds: int = DEFAULT_GEOCODE_CACHE_TTL_SECONDS,
    key_prefix: str = DEFAULT_GEOCODE_CACHE_KEY_PREFIX,
    cache_misses: bool = False,
)

    A :class:~tempest_fastapi_sdk.geo.GeocodingBackend that answers from a cache.

    Wraps any backend — :class:~tempest_fastapi_sdk.geo.NominatimBackend being the one worth wrapping — and consults store before touching the network. Parameters are keyword-only.

    Privacy: reverse rounds the coordinate to precision places before building the key and before calling the wrapped backend, so the exact GPS reading never leaves the process — not in the key, not on the wire. geocode keys by a SHA-256 of the trimmed, casefolded query, so the text a user typed never appears in a key either.

    Failure policy: any exception from store.get/store.set is logged at WARNING and the lookup continues as if the cache were empty — the cache is quota protection, not a source of truth. An exception from the wrapped backend propagates unchanged.

    Attributes:

    Name Type Description
    precision int

    Decimal places used to round the coordinate.
    ttl_seconds int

    Lifetime given to every entry this backend writes.
    key_prefix str

    First segment of every key it builds.
    cache_misses bool

    Whether "the backend found nothing" is cached too.

    Wrap a backend with a cache in front of it.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    backend GeocodingBackend

    Where to go on a miss. Its exceptions are the caller's to handle, unchanged.

    		 required
    store GeocodeCacheStore

    Where entries live. Any object with the two :class:GeocodeCacheStore methods.

    		 required
    precision int

    Decimal places of the coordinate rounding in reverse (3 ≈ 111 m, 4 ≈ 11 m, 5 ≈ 1 m). The rounded value is both the key and what the backend is asked.

    		 DEFAULT_GEOCODE_CACHE_PRECISION
    ttl_seconds int

    Lifetime of each entry. Defaults to 30 days (:data:DEFAULT_GEOCODE_CACHE_TTL_SECONDS), long enough that a device fleet settles into hits and short enough that a corrected place is not pinned forever.

    		 DEFAULT_GEOCODE_CACHE_TTL_SECONDS
    key_prefix str

    Namespace for every key (<prefix>:reverse:v1:… / <prefix>:search:v1:…).

    		 DEFAULT_GEOCODE_CACHE_KEY_PREFIX
    cache_misses bool

    When True, a None answer is stored as the empty string too, so "nobody can find this place" stops costing a request. Default False: an answer that may change (a new place opening) is re-asked, and the rare miss is not worth caching.

    		 False

    GeocodeCacheStore ¶

    Bases: Protocol

    Where :class:CachedGeocodingBackend keeps serialized answers.

    Both methods deal in strings: the value is a JSON payload, so anything that can hold text can be a store — Redis, an in-process dict, the cache a service already runs. Implement the two methods and the wrapper does the rest.

    InMemoryGeocodeCacheStore ¶

    InMemoryGeocodeCacheStore()

    A :class:GeocodeCacheStore holding entries in this process.

    Expiry is checked on read against :func:time.monotonic, so a wall-clock adjustment never keeps an entry alive or kills one early. The methods do not await, so under asyncio there is no interleaving point and no lock is needed. State is per worker: reach for :class:RedisGeocodeCacheStore the moment more than one process serves traffic.

    Start with an empty store.

    paginate_nearby async ¶

    paginate_nearby(
    center: Coordinate,
    radius_km: float,
    *,
    page: int = 1,
    page_size: int = 20,
    extra_filters: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
    query: Select[Any] | None = None,
    where: WhereClause | None = None,
    latitude_field: str = "latitude",
    longitude_field: str = "longitude",
) -> dict[str, Any]

    Return one page of rows within radius_km, nearest first, in SQL.

    Where :meth:nearby loads the whole bounding box and sorts in Python — so paginating it means paginating in memory — this method keeps everything in the database: the distance is :func:haversine_distance_sql, the radius is a WHERE on it (behind the indexable bounding-box pre-filter), and the sort, COUNT and OFFSET / LIMIT all run there. Ties on distance break on id, so pages stay stable.

    Rows whose latitude or longitude is NULL never match. The bounding box is clamped at the antimeridian, exactly as in :meth:nearby, so a circle crossing longitude ±180 misses the far side.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    center Coordinate

    The circle centre.

    		 required
    radius_km float

    The inclusive radius in kilometres.

    PostGISRepositoryMixin ¶

    Repository mixin whose radius search runs entirely in PostGIS.

    LivePositionStore(

    *,
    key_prefix: str = DEFAULT_LIVE_POSITION_KEY_PREFIX,
    ttl_seconds: int = DEFAULT_LIVE_POSITION_TTL_SECONDS,
    min_interval_seconds: float = DEFAULT_LIVE_POSITION_INTERVAL_SECONDS,
    min_distance_m: float = DEFAULT_LIVE_POSITION_MIN_DISTANCE_M,
    broker: SSEBroker | None = None,
    audience: AudienceResolver | None = None,

    cleared_event_name: str = DEFAULT_LIVE_POSITION_CLEARED_EVENT,
    eta_targets: EtaTargetsResolver | None = None,
    routing: RoutingBackend | None = None,
    mode: TravelModeEnum = CAR,
    clock: Callable[[], float] = time,
)

    Latest position per channel in Redis, delivered to a resolved audience.

    Takes the client rather than a manager: pass AsyncRedisManager.client_proxy when the store is built before the lifespan runs, or AsyncRedisManager.client once inside.

    The acceptance check reads the previous position and then writes the new one, two round trips with no lock between them. Two positions for the same channel arriving at the same instant can both pass the throttle; that costs one extra event, never a wrong position, and a channel has a single sender in the use this is built for.

    Attributes:

    Name Type Description
    key_prefix str

    First segment of every key.
    ttl_seconds int

    Lifetime of the latest position.
    min_interval_seconds float

    Throttle between accepted positions.
    min_distance_m float

    Least movement for a position to be accepted.
    event_name str

    SSE event name of an accepted position.
    cleared_event_name str

    SSE event name :meth:clear sends.
    mode TravelModeEnum

    Travel mode of the ETA.

    Initialize the store.

    publish async ¶

    publish(channel_id: str, position: LivePositionSchema) -> bool

    Keep position as the latest of channel_id when it is worth it.

    Refused, in order, when: it is not newer than the stored one (recorded_at not after it — a late or replayed fix); less than min_interval_seconds of server time passed since the last accepted one; it moved less than min_distance_m. A position refused for distance still renews the TTL, so a sender standing at a stop does not vanish. An accepted position is written with the TTL and, with a broker, delivered to the audience.

    The channel (trip, delivery, vehicle).

    RoadMatchOptions dataclass ¶

    RoadMatchOptions(
    sigma_m: float = 7.0,
    beta_m: float = 3.0,
    radius_m: float = 200.0,
    max_candidates: int = 16,
    max_detour_m: float = 100.0,
    detour_per_second_m: float = 2.0,
    max_interval_s: float = 60.0,
    min_spacing_m: float | None = None,
)

    Tuning of the hidden Markov model behind :func:match_to_roads.

    Attributes:

    Name Type Description
    sigma_m float

    GPS noise, standard deviation in metres.
    beta_m float

    Scale of the transition, in metres: a move costs |straight - network| / beta_m.
    radius_m float

    Roads farther than this from a fix are not candidates.
    max_candidates int

    At most this many nearest roads per fix.
    max_detour_m float

    A transition whose network distance exceeds the straight line by more than this is impossible; bounds the shortest-path search.
    detour_per_second_m float

    Extra detour allowed per second between two timed fixes, in metres: the bound becomes straight + max_detour_m + detour_per_second_m * min(dt, max_interval_s). A sparse source (a fix every 5-30 s) turns corners and goes round blocks between fixes, so a bound fixed for 1 Hz breaks the chain on real drives. Applies only when both fixes have a timestamp; 0 turns it off.
    max_interval_s float

    Intervals longer than this, in seconds, grant no more detour: the slack stops at detour_per_second_m * max_interval_s.
    min_spacing_m float | None

    A fix closer than this to the previous kept fix skips the model. None is 2 * sigma_m.

    spacing_m property ¶

    spacing_m: float

    The pre-filter distance actually used.

    Returns:

    Name Type Description
    float float

    min_spacing_m, or 2 * sigma_m when unset.

    QualityHistogram ¶

    QualityHistogram(bounds: Sequence[float])

    A histogram with fixed buckets: memory independent of the count.

    Buckets are right-closed: (bounds[i - 1], bounds[i]]; values above the last bound go to one overflow bucket. :meth:quantile answers by nearest rank (the same rule as tempest-react-sdk's benchmarks) with the upper bound of the bucket holding that rank, clamped to the largest value seen — so it overestimates by less than one bucket width, and is exact for values that sit on a bound.

    Attributes:

    Name Type Description
    bounds tuple[float, ...]

    Upper bounds, increasing.
    counts list[int]

    One count per bucket plus the overflow.
    total int

    Values added.
    largest float

    Largest value added (-inf when empty).

    Start empty.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    bounds Sequence[float]

    Bucket upper bounds, increasing.

    Type Description

    RoadGraph(
    nodes: Sequence[Coordinate], edges: Sequence[RoadEdge], *, two_way: bool = False
)

    A road network ready for matching: nodes, edges, index and adjacency.

    Build it once per region and reuse it for every trace — building is the expensive part; querying is cheap. The plane is equirectangular around the centre of the nodes' bounding box: within a city the scale error is a fraction of a percent. Graphs that cross the antimeridian are not supported — split them.

    route_through async ¶

    route_through(
    points: Sequence[Coordinate],
    *,
    mode: TravelModeEnum = CAR,
    with_geometry: bool = False,
) -> RouteThroughResult

    Fetch one road route through every point, in order, in one request.

    Sends all points to OSRM's /route service, which answers the whole route plus one leg per consecutive pair. Distances are used as-is; every duration (total and per leg) is multiplied by the mode's duration factor, exactly like :meth:route. The legs carry no geometry; with_geometry=True decodes the full route polyline into :attr:RouteThroughResult.geometry.

    Parameters:

    The ordered points (origin, stops, destination). Between 2 and :attr:max_points.

    RouteThroughResult

    If fewer than two points, or more than :attr:max_points, are given. Raised before any request.

    Fetch a many-to-many distance/duration matrix in one request.

    BoundingBox ¶

    Bases: BaseSchema

    GeocodeAddress ¶

    Bases: BaseSchema

    Structured address parts of a resolved place.

    Parsed from the address object a Nominatim entry carries when the request asks for addressdetails=1. Every field is optional: the backend returns only what it knows about the matched place, so a coordinate in open country can yield a country and nothing else.

    Attributes:

    Name Type Description
    city str | None

    Municipality-level name. Nominatim spells it under four different keys — city, town, village and municipality — and a single entry can carry several at once (a village inside its town), so this is the first key present in that order, largest settlement first. Measured on payloads from nominatim.openstreetmap.org: Teresina/PI answers city, Coivaras/PI answers town, São José da Tenda/PI answers town alongside village and hamlet.
    state str | None

    First-level subdivision name (e.g. "Piauí"), from address.state.
    state_code str | None

    Short subdivision code, the part after the - of address["ISO3166-2-lvl4"] ("BR-PI" → "PI"). None when the key is absent or carries no separator. A string, not an enum: the geocoder is worldwide.
    country str | None

    Country name as spelled by the backend ("Brasil"), from address.country.
    country_code str | None

    ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code uppercased ("br" → "BR"), from address.country_code.
    postcode str | None

    Postal code of the place, from address.postcode.

    TrafficPrivacy dataclass ¶

    TrafficPrivacy(
    min_devices: int = 5,
    window_seconds: int = 300,
    trim_radius_m: float = 200.0,
    trip_gap_seconds: float = 300.0,
    max_accuracy_m: float = 50.0,
    max_speed_kmh: float = 200.0,
    min_edge_coverage_m: float = 10.0,
)

    The privacy and cleaning rules of a :class:TrafficAggregator.

    The distinct-device count of an edge is taken per salt epoch (each epoch is window_seconds long and has its own salt) and the window's count is the largest of the epochs it overlaps: hashes of two epochs never match, so adding them would count a device twice; the maximum can only under-count.

    Attributes:

    Name Type Description
    min_devices int

    k of k-anonymity: an edge is published only when this many distinct devices drove it in the window.
    window_seconds int

    Sliding window of the snapshot, and the life of each hash salt.
    trim_radius_m float

    Positions this close to the start of a trip, or to where the device is when the trip ends, are never aggregated.
    trip_gap_seconds float

    Silence after which a device's trip is over (its pending stretch is dropped) and the next position starts a new one.
    max_accuracy_m float

    Positions reporting a worse accuracy_m are dropped.
    max_speed_kmh float

    A position implying a faster move from the previous kept one is an outlier and is dropped; speed samples above it are discarded.
    min_edge_coverage_m float

    Least distance driven on an edge for a pass to become a speed sample.

The parser receives a date, not a clock, so it sets no time: the caller keeps only the trips that leave from its own current time on. An explicit date in the phrase wins: one other than today ("agora ... amanhã") or one that does not exist makes this False, while one that falls on today ("hoje agora") keeps it True.

    resolve_br_coordinate async ¶

    resolve_br_coordinate(
    *,
    geocoder: GeocodingBackend | None,
    uf: UFEnum | str,
    address: str | None = None,
    city: str | None = None,
    complement: str | None = None,
    country: str = "Brasil",
) -> Coordinate | None

    Resolve the best known point for a Brazilian address.

    Tries three sources, most precise first, and returns the first that answers:

    1. the CEP found in address or complement (see :func:extract_cep), through :func:cep_to_coordinate;
    2. the full address — "address, city, UFEnum, country" with the empty parts left out — geocoded as one query (skipped when both address and city are empty);
    3. the state centroid (:func:uf_centroid), offline, which always answers for a valid UFEnum.

    A geocoder failure is not an error here: any exception from geocoder.geocode is logged at WARNING (with the traceback) and the chain moves to the next step, so the worst outcome is the state centroid. Retrying belongs on the geocoder you inject — wrap its geocode with :func:~tempest_fastapi_sdk.async_retry — because this function only sees the failure after your retries are spent.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default

    haversine_distance_sql ¶

    haversine_distance_sql(
    latitude: SQLColumnExpression[float],
    longitude: SQLColumnExpression[float],
    center: Coordinate,
) -> ColumnElement[float]

    Build the Haversine great-circle distance as a SQL expression.

    Uses only sin, cos, asin and sqrt plus arithmetic — no PostGIS, no radians() (degrees are converted by multiplying with a bound constant). Plain PostgreSQL has all four; SQLite has them when built with its math functions (SQLITE_ENABLE_MATH_FUNCTIONS, SQLite 3.35+). Check yours with SELECT sin(1), asin(1), sqrt(4); the SQLite 3.47.1 inside the CPython 3.13.3 that uv installs answers it.

    The haversine term is clamped to [0, 1] with a CASE before sqrt / asin. Floating-point error pushes it past 1: for random antipodal pairs it came out as 1.0000000000000002 in about 4% of 2,000,000 draws on PostgreSQL 16, and on SQLite 3.47.1 too. sqrt happens to round that value back to 1.0, so neither engine failed in those draws — but asin of anything above 1 is NULL on SQLite and ERROR: input is out of range on PostgreSQL (both measured), and the clamp keeps the result from depending on that rounding. The centre's cosine is computed in Python and bound, so each row pays one cos.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    latitude SQLColumnExpression[float]

    The latitude column (or expression), in degrees.

    		 required
    longitude SQLColumnExpression[float]

    The longitude column (or expression), in degrees.

    		 required
    center Coordinate

    The point distances are measured from.

    		 required

    Returns:

    Type Description
    ColumnElement[float]

    ColumnElement[float]: The distance in kilometres, same formula and
    ColumnElement[float]

    Earth radius (:data:~tempest_fastapi_sdk.geo.EARTH_RADIUS_KM) as
    ColumnElement[float]

    match_to_roads ¶

    match_to_roads(
    fixes: Sequence[Coordinate],
    graph: RoadGraph,
    options: RoadMatchOptions = ROAD_MATCH_DEFAULTS,
    *,
    timestamps: Sequence[float | None] | None = None,
) -> RoadMatchResult

    Match a GPS trace to a road network (Newson & Krumm 2009).

    • Breaks: when no transition is possible (a gap, a missing road), the chain restarts at that fix instead of failing; routes gets one entry per chain and breaks counts them.
    • Close fixes (within the spacing of the last kept one) skip the model and are projected onto that fix's edge, inferred=True.
    • No road in reach: the match is None and the fix counts in unmatched; it does not break the chain.
    • Sparse fixes: pass timestamps and the detour allowed between two fixes grows by detour_per_second_m per second of interval (capped at max_interval_s). Without them the bound is the fixed max_detour_m, tuned for 1 Hz, and a fix every 5-30 s breaks the chain where the vehicle turned a corner or went round a block in between. A missing (None) or nan time, a repeated one or one that goes back grants no slack, so an untimed trace gives exactly the result it gave before.

    Synchronous and CPU-bound; from async code run it with asyncio.to_thread when the trace is long.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    fixes Sequence[Coordinate]

    The trace, in time order.

    		 required
    graph RoadGraph

    The network.

    		 required
    options RoadMatchOptions

    Model tuning; defaults in :data:ROAD_MATCH_DEFAULTS.

    		 ROAD_MATCH_DEFAULTS
    timestamps Sequence[float | None] | None

    Capture time of each fix, epoch seconds (datetime.timestamp()), same length as fixes; None for a fix without one.

    		 None

    The match of every fix, the route, and what was

    Type Description

    When timestamps does not have one entry per fix.

    find_municipalities_in_text ¶

    find_municipalities_in_text(
    text: str, *, limit: int | None = 5, cutoff: float = 0.85, min_score: float = 0.6
) -> list[MunicipalityMatch]

    Find the municipalities a free-form text mentions.

    Every run of up to :data:MAX_NAME_TOKENS words is looked up, exactly first and then with typos (cutoff). A state written right after the name ("Campinas/SP", "Campinas - São Paulo", "campinas SP") keeps only the homonyms in that state and marks them uf_confirmed; a state written there that the name does not exist in drops the match. Overlapping matches keep the best (longer on a tie), so "são josé dos campos" is one city, not São José plus Campos; and the words of a state that confirmed a match are not a city of their own, so "Campinas, São Paulo" is Campinas alone.

    Scores: the name similarity, times 0.9 when no state confirms it, times :data:UNCUED_SINGLE_WORD_FACTOR for a one-word name that does not look like a place ("estou feliz").

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    text str

    What the user wrote.

    		 required
    limit int | None

    Most matches to return; None for all.

    infer_road_candidates ¶

    infer_road_candidates(
    density: OffRoadDensity,
    graph: RoadGraph,
    *,
    min_points: int = 3,
    min_length_m: float = 40.0,
    min_novel_fraction: float = 0.8,
    connect_m: float | None = None,
) -> list[RoadCandidateSchema]

    Turn committed off-road density into road candidates for review.

    Cells with at least min_points positions are closed (3x3), thinned (Zhang-Suen), traced into lines between junctions, simplified (Douglas-Peucker at one cell), joined at each end to the road within connect_m and kept when at least min_length_m long and at least min_novel_fraction of the line is farther than density.off_road_m from every road of graph.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    density OffRoadDensity

    Committed density (only k-anonymous cells).

    		 required
    graph RoadGraph

    The base network the candidates are diffed against.

    		 required
    min_points int

    Least positions for a cell to count.

    		 3
    min_length_m float

    Shorter lines are dropped (spurs, noise).

    		 40.0
    min_novel_fraction float

    Least share of the line off every road.

    		 0.8
    connect_m float | None

    An end of a line within this distance of a road is extended to its projection on that road, so the candidate shows where it joins the network (the stretch near a crossing street is never off-road, so the density alone stops short of it). None is 2 * density.off_road_m; 0 disables it.

    		 None

    Returns:

    Type Description
    list[RoadCandidateSchema]

    list[RoadCandidateSchema]: Candidates, longest first.

    parse_trip_intent ¶

    parse_trip_intent(
    text: str,
    today: date,
    *,
    municipalities: Iterable[Municipality] | TripCityIndex | None = None,
) -> TripIntent

    Read origin, destination, date and part of the day from a trip phrase.

    Origin and destination come from prepositions and verbs ("de X", "pra Y", "saindo de X", "indo para Y", "X pra Y"); without them, the cities said count in order (first origin, second destination), by exact name only. Dates: hoje, amanhã, depois de amanhã, a weekday ("próxima sexta", "sexta que vem"), "dia 20", "dia 20 de outubro", "20/10"; periods: madrugada, manhã, tarde, noite. A "leave now" phrase ("agora", "já", "o quanto antes"...) with no other date is today, with :attr:TripIntent.departure_now set.

    The cities that may be recognized. None is the whole country. A service passes the cities it serves (or a prebuilt :func:build_trip_city_index, reused across phrases), and a real city outside them comes back in unrecognized.

    Most points :meth:OSRMBackend.route_through sends in one request.

    Matches the public demo at router.project-osrm.org, measured on 2026-11-18: a /route request with 500 coordinates answered "Ok" and one with 501 answered {"code": "TooBig", "message": "Number of entries 501 is higher than current maximum (500)"}. A self-hosted osrm-routed sets its own cap with --max-viaroute-size; pass max_points to :class:OSRMBackend to match it, so the refusal is a local ValueError naming the limit instead of a round trip that fails.

    DEFAULT_GEOCODE_CACHE_PRECISION: int = 3

    Decimal places a reverse coordinate is rounded to before keying.

    Three places is a ~111 m grid (measured with :func:~tempest_fastapi_sdk.geo.haversine_km at 10⁻³ of a degree of latitude); more places fragment the cache without making the answer better, since a street resolves to the same building.

    DEFAULT_GEOCODE_CACHE_TTL_SECONDS module-attribute ¶

    DEFAULT_GEOCODE_CACHE_TTL_SECONDS: int = 2592000

    Default entry lifetime: 30 days.

    Long enough that a whole device fleet settles into hits, short enough that a map edit or a corrected place reaches users within a month. Place resolutions are stable on that horizon — the coordinates of a doorway do not move — while a week would re-buy quota every month and "forever" would pin a wrong answer.

    UNCUED_SINGLE_WORD_FACTOR module-attribute ¶

    UNCUED_SINGLE_WORD_FACTOR: float = 0.5

    Score factor for a one-word match with no sign of being a place.

    "Feliz", "Natal" and "Alegre" are municipalities and everyday words. A lowercase single word with no locative cue before it (:data:LOCATIVE_CUES), no state after it, and other words around it is kept at half the score, so "estou feliz" ranks below the default min_score while "moro em feliz", "Feliz/RS" and a text that is only "feliz" (a form's city field) do not.

    CEP_PATTERN module-attribute ¶

    CEP_PATTERN: Pattern[str] = re.compile('\\b(\\d{5})-?(\\d{3})\\b')

    A CEP written anywhere in free text, with or without the dash.

    Word boundaries on both ends keep it from matching eight digits inside a longer run (a phone number, a document number): "123456789" does not match, "CEP 01310-100, sala 4" does.

    LIVE_POSITION_MAX_CLOCK_SKEW module-attribute ¶

    LIVE_POSITION_MAX_CLOCK_SKEW: Final[timedelta] = timedelta(seconds=30)

    How far in the future recorded_at may be before it is refused.

    A phone's clock drifts a few seconds from the server's; refusing anything strictly ahead of now would drop honest positions. Thirty seconds absorbs that drift and still refuses a timestamp that is plainly wrong.

    ROAD_MATCH_DEFAULTS module-attribute ¶

    ROAD_MATCH_DEFAULTS: Final[RoadMatchOptions] = RoadMatchOptions()

    Default tuning: sigma 7 m, beta 3 m, radius 200 m, 16 roads, detour 100 m, plus 2 m of detour per second between timed fixes, capped at 60 s.

    Ported from tempest-react-sdk's ROAD_MATCH_DEFAULTS, chosen there by sweeping every knob on the Kubicka et al. dataset (100 real drives, 247 251 fixes, node scripts/bench-map-matching.mjs): 92.33% of fixes on the right road, 98.53% without the three drives through yards missing from OSM.

    detour_per_second_m and max_interval_s were chosen there on the same drives thinned to one fix every 5-300 s and on public OpenStreetMap traces of five Brazilian city centres (node scripts/bench-br-osm.mjs, PR #678): 2 m/s is the largest rate that leaves the 1 Hz result where it was, and a 60 s cap keeps the long gaps of a 1 Hz trace from widening the search.

    Value of a declared dimension the app did not give for a trip.

    DEFAULT_DENSITY_CELL_M module-attribute ¶

    DEFAULT_DENSITY_CELL_M: Final[float] = 5.0

    Side of a density cell, metres: finer than a lane, coarser than GPS noise.

    DEFAULT_DENSITY_BLOCK_CELLS module-attribute ¶

    DEFAULT_DENSITY_BLOCK_CELLS: Final[int] = 5

    Side of a k-anonymity block, in cells: 5 x 5 m = 25 m.

    k is decided per block, not per 5 m cell: with GPS noise a device spreads its points over several cells across the road, so k distinct devices in one 5 m cell is rare where k in a 25 m block is not. Measured on the synthetic street of scripts/bench_geo_traffic.py (k 5, sigma 5 m): deciding per cell, 20 trips a day gave no candidate and 40 recovered the street; per block, 12 trips recover 77% of it and 20 all of it. Counts stay per cell.

    DEFAULT_DENSITY_EPOCH_SECONDS module-attribute ¶

    DEFAULT_DENSITY_EPOCH_SECONDS: Final[int] = 86400

    Epoch of the density hashes: one day, then only counts remain.

    DEFAULT_OFF_ROAD_M module-attribute ¶

    DEFAULT_OFF_ROAD_M: Final[float] = 20.0

    Distance from every road beyond which a position counts as off-road.

    The phase-0 measurement of tempest-react-sdk#667 (Kubicka et al., 247 251 fixes) found 9.4% of fixes farther than 20 m from any road of their OSM excerpt, and 90.6% within it: the raw signal of a road the base lacks.
